sample.topic: Weekly ticket sales report of Vizney Live, a fictional US live entertainment company (32 shows in Los Angeles, New York and Chicago), built from the parts Netflix shows data with instead of charts (the billboard, a Top 10 of outlined numerals with bars and rank moves, weeks in the Top 10, the continue-watching progress bar, the episode list, the hover card, the TOP 10 badge and the FAQ accordion) in one card and chart grammar on a dark page

canvas.role: page background, header and footer (netflix.com's signed-out pages are black, measured)

card.role: every figure, table and the workbench: no border, no shadow, an 8px radius (the dark step behind the landing's rails; Tudum's page is #242424)

plot.role: chart background: the card itself, never a second panel

raise.role: the hover card (tooltip) and the Top 10 poster (measured: #232323, 8px radius)

field.role: FAQ rows (measured: #2d2d2d, 24px padding, 8px apart), install-command boxes; the hover band behind a bar is #262626

hair.role: the fill of the outlined Top 10 numerals (measured #414141), chart baselines

line.role: chart gridlines and the workbench dividers

rule.role: rules between table rows and between episode rows (the episode list divider)

ink.role: titles, key figures, table values, the current week's tick, the focus ring

body.role: running text, code, labels inside dark cells

text-2.role: subtitles, figure labels, KPI labels, footer text: rgba(255,255,255,.7) on black, as netflix.com and Tudum set secondary text (8.6:1 on the card)

muted.role: notes, axis ticks, table headers, captions under tiles (4.6:1 on the card: the lightest gray for small text, and only on #161616 or darker; use text-2 on #232323 and lighter)

accent.role: Netflix red for UI only (measured #e50914): the primary button, the TOP 10 badge, the NEW ribbon, the selected code tab. White text on it is 4.8:1. Data takes its own red step, #f0313b

gray-button.role: the secondary button: rgba(128,128,128,.4) with white text, 40px, 16px/500, padding 6px 16px, 4px radius (measured: 'Learn more' on netflix.com/kr); hover at .6

good.role: favourable change, text only (the green Netflix uses for match scores, 9.3:1 on the card)

bad.role: unfavourable change, text only (orange, so it never reads as the red subject; 6.3:1 on the card)

validation.tool: dataviz validate_palette.js (OKLab), mode dark, on the card #161616 where every chart sits
validation.categorical: red #f0313b (one step lighter than the UI red #e50914, which stays on buttons and badges) and blue #6a88f2 (netflix.com's blue #4061e7 raised for a dark surface) pass every check: CVD ΔE 27.6 (deutan), normal vision 32.8, OKLCH lightness inside the dark band 0.48–0.67, contrast 4.49 and 5.53:1. Two hues on purpose: Netflix paints with red and keeps the rest gray
validation.other: #595959 is a neutral gray one step above the numeral fill #414141; neutral by design (lightness band and chroma floor do not apply). Against red: CVD 7.4 (protan), normal 24.9 against blue. At 2.58:1 it always has a second cue: a 2px gap between segments, value labels and a table
validation.comparison: #808080 against red: 4.58:1 on the card, always dashed (6 4) and labeled at its end
validation.sequential: one red hue (#9e2027 → #ffa3a7, dim to bright, because on a dark card a larger value is brighter): monotone lightness, every gap ≥ 0.06, the dim end 2.32:1, hue spread 8°
validation.diverging: arms #ffa3a7→#9e2027 and #b3c3f9→#3f55a8 each pass the ordinal checks (dim ends 2.32 and 2.65:1, hue spread 8° and 2°); poles CVD 11.7 (protan), normal 15.1; the midpoint #3a3a3a is a neutral that sinks into the card
validation.status: good #46d369 9.3:1 and bad #e87c03 6.3:1 as text on the card; status is never color alone: a change keeps its sign and its comparison words
validation.text: label steps on the card: red text #ff5a63 5.9:1, blue text #8ea5f6 7.6:1; digits in grid cells are #e5e5e5 on #333333 (9.6:1) and black on the red #1 cell (5.2:1)

code.note: the screen's own text steps (blue keyword, green string, orange number, red function), all ≥ 4.5:1 on #0b0b0b

sans.role: everything: Roboto stands in for Netflix Sans (it is in netflix.com's own fallback stack: 'Netflix Sans', 'Helvetica Neue', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Ubuntu, sans-serif); netflix.com loads Netflix Sans 400, 500 and 700, Tudum's ranks use 900. Netflix Sans has no Hangul, so Korean pages fall back to system fonts and Korean uses Pretendard

numeral.size: 58px in the Top 10 (netflix.com: 100px over a 252px poster)

rows: black header 72px: company and report name; period, EN/KO, Export PDF (outlined), Copy as Markdown (red)
filter row: outlined chips, the selected one white
billboard: TOP 10 badge and the #1 line, the headline, a lede, a red and a gray button, four key figures; key art is a color block with a giant outlined numeral
This week: Figure 1 Top 10 (12, two columns of five rows); Figure 2 tickets by week (7) · Figure 3 weeks in the Top 10 (5)
Coming up: Figure 4 episode list with progress bars (7) · Figure 5 channels (5); Table 1 every show (12)
How it's built: three gradient step cards, then the window (package 240px · figure and checks · code)
Method and sources: the FAQ accordion

tableau.fonts: Tableau Book for text; Roboto only if it is installed on every viewing machine and the server

measured.landing: body #000000; text #ffffff and rgba(255,255,255,.7); h1 56px/700 (line-height 70px); row titles 24px/500; primary button #e50914, 4px radius (header 32px 14px/500 4px 16px; hero 56px 24px/500 12px 24px); secondary rgba(128,128,128,.4) 40px 16px/500 6px 16px; Trending Now posters #232323, 8px radius, 180×252, numerals 100px/700 #414141 with a 4px white stroke and a 24px black glow over the poster's lower left; feature cards linear-gradient(149deg, #192247 0%, #210e17 96.86%), 16px radius, titles 24px/500, text rgba(255,255,255,.7); FAQ rows #2d2d2d, 24px/400, 24px padding, 8px apart; the curved divider #210d16 → #b82869 → #e50914 with a rgba(64,97,231,.4) glow; footer rgba(255,255,255,.7) 14px
measured.tudum: rank '01' 36px/900 white; header 14px/500 white; rows 18px/400 with a 16:9 thumbnail and no rules; weeks in the Top 10 as a plain integer; views and hours in full digits (10,700,000); runtime h:mm (1:48); week as 10/19/26 - 10/25/26; filters as 40px 4px-radius buttons, 14px
measured.fonts: Netflix Sans 400, 500, 700 loaded on the landing (fallback 'Helvetica Neue', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Ubuntu, sans-serif); no Hangul subset
